one_month_reasoning: Scheduled events in the window: (1) ASML Q3 2026 results on Wednesday 2026-10-14, now confirmed (source 25). Q3 guidance was EUR 11-12bn at 55-57% GM (source 1) and consensus is EUR 11.68bn (source 15), so the print itself is expected. What can move the stock is the first 2027 view and bookings. Management has already said 2027 Low-NA capacity is close to fully booked, and 2027 consensus revenue of EUR 54.6bn (+27%) already reflects that. (2) The late-October FOMC meeting. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (source 21), and Polymarket puts another 2026 hike at 78% (source 18), so a hawkish surprise mostly hits high-multiple names. (3) Any NDAA/MATCH Act movement: the Senate bill has been stalled since its failed July cloture vote (source 24), so passage inside October is unlikely. Base rates from 20 years of ASML monthly data (source 4): the 1-month return has a 10th-90th percentile range of -9% to +14% and a median of +1.8%. October returns (the Q3-report month) over 2006-2025 have a median of about +1.7% with a range of -19% (2024, booking miss) to +21%. The stock has also just recovered from the AI-pacing selloff in mid-September (source 22). So I see no strong directional edge: I centre the distribution at about 1,815 (+0.4%) with about 12.5% monthly vol and fat tails (Student-t, 5 df), giving P(>=spot) 0.515.

fair_value.method: Blend of four methods. 2027E EPS EUR 51.73 (USD 58.17 at 1.1244) x 34x = USD 1,978 (weight 0.40). 2028E EPS EUR 60, cut 3.5% for the probability-weighted MATCH Act risk to EUR 57.9 (USD 65.1), x 30x = USD 1,953 (weight 0.35). A base-rate anchor of spot x (1 + 2.5%) = USD 1,854, which blends ASML's own conditional median after +50% run-ups (+13%) with peer AMAT's (-22%) at 70/30 (weight 0.15). The mean analyst target of USD 2,116 (weight 0.10). Blended: USD 1,965.

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo Finance average of 33 analysts (range 37.43-59.10), confirmed in EUR; it matches StockAnalysis at 51.72 and 24/7 Wall St. In round 1 this came only from a search snippet; it is now verified on two data pages.

The 10-year trailing P/E median is 37.2 (GuruFocus) and the 10-year average is 37.13 (FullRatio). I take about 3 turns below the median, versus 2 turns in round 1, because the Fed is now hiking (to 3.75-4.00% with more priced, sources 21 and 18), 2027 would be the third WFE up-year, and peer equipment stocks de-rated after comparable run-ups (source 26).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: 2028E EPS EUR 60 x (1 - 3.5% MATCH Act expected haircut) = EUR 57.9 = USD 65.1; x 30x NTM as priced in Oct 2027

inputs_detail.derivation: 2027E EUR 51.73 grown about 16%. SEMI now forecasts WFE +14.1% in 2028 (source 11). Citi sees TSMC capex at $77bn in 2027 and $86bn in 2028 (+12%, source 29). ASML is investigating a further +30% EUV capacity step for 2028 (source 1). EUV mix and operating leverage carry EPS growth slightly above WFE growth.

China is about 20% of 2026 sales (source 32). A full DUV-immersion sales and servicing ban would cut roughly 10% of 2028 EPS after redeploying tools to other customers. I put about a 35% chance on enactment and Dutch alignment affecting 2028: it rides the Senate NDAA (source 23), but Senate cloture failed and the bill is stalled (source 24). 0.35 x 10% = 3.5%.

The forward P/E was about 28x at $1,575 in mid-September (source 32) and is about 31x on 2027E today. With 2028 growth of about 15%, below 2027's about 35%, 30x is near the low end of the 10-year trailing range of 22-64 (median 37), which suits a late-cycle year.

bear.story: AI capex digestion (the AI-pacing call of 2026-09-14 was an early warning; Polymarket prices an 'AI bubble burst' by mid-2027 at 17.5% on thin volume), plus Fed hikes compressing multiples and/or the MATCH Act passing in the NDAA. 2028 EUV orders get pushed out, and EPS is flat to down in 2028 at about 21-23x. This mirrors AMAT's -22% to -38% after the 2021 and 2024 run-ups and ASML's 2022 (-57%) and 2024-25 (-45%) drawdowns.

base.story: 2026 lands at EUR 43-45bn and 2027 grows about 25% with EUV sold out. Hyperscaler capex keeps rising (S&P Global: about $1.3tn in 2027; Manifold 85% that big-4 capex exceeds $600bn). The market rolls to 2028 EPS of about EUR 58-60 at about 29-30x; the June 2027 Capital Markets Day lifts the 2030 framework modestly. The return is a few percent, between ASML's own conditional base rate (+13%) and the peer base rate (negative).

bull.story: The AI build-out extends into 2028-29: TSMC capex heads to $86-90bn, the 2028 +30% EUV capacity step is confirmed, High-NA moves into production and the Capital Markets Day raises 2030 above EUR 60bn. The MATCH Act stalls, recession is avoided (Kalshi 21%), and the multiple holds at about 33-35x on 2028 EPS of EUR 65+.

thesis_break_reason: A close near USD 1,250 (-31%) is about 21.5x 2027E EPS of USD 58.17, at the floor of the 10-year P/E range (21.95), and just below the March-2026 low (1,248.11 intramonth, source 4). Trading there would most likely mean the market had stopped believing in 2027-28 EUV growth: an order push-out or cancellation cycle as hyperscalers or labs slow AI build-outs, enactment of a DUV sales-and-servicing ban on China (MATCH Act), or a rate-driven de-rating with a cyclical downturn. Ordinary volatility (about 13% a month) does not usually take the stock that far without a fundamental cause.

reasoning: Continuation of round 1 with the search budget restored (about 25 more lookups). Base rates recomputed from 20 years of ASML monthly closes (source 4): the unconditional forward 12m median is +27% (75% positive, 5th-95th percentile -31%/+105%). After a trailing gain above +50%, the median falls to +13% (72% positive). After a trailing gain above +80% (today +87%), it is 0% (56% positive), but that is only 4 independent episodes (2009-10 up, 2013 flat, 2019 up, 2021 down). New peer evidence (source 26): AMAT fell 1-38% in the 12 months after each +60-190% run-up in 2017, 2021 and 2024, and rose only after 2019. So the peer base rate is clearly worse than ASML's own, and I now blend in some of it. Macro and event odds: Kalshi's 2027 recession contract is 21% (deep market) against Polymarket's 34.5% (thin), which is better than I assumed in round 1. But the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and Polymarket gives 78% to another 2026 hike, a valuation headwind. Taiwan invasion by mid-2027 is at 8.5%, and 'AI bubble burst' is at 8% for 2026 (deep) and 17.5% by June 2027 (thin). New bear evidence: the 2026-09-14 AI-pacing call (Amodei, with Altman and xAI concurring) knocked 5-6% off equipment stocks. The MATCH Act would ban DUV-immersion sales and servicing in China and rides the Senate NDAA, though the Senate is stalled. New bull evidence: SEMI's mid-year forecast has WFE +21.8% in 2027 and +14.1% in 2028; TSMC 2026 capex is $60-64bn with Citi at $77bn for 2027; S&P Global sees about $1.3tn of hyperscaler capex in 2027; and a June 2027 Capital Markets Day is a likely upside catalyst. Verified facts: 2027E EPS of EUR 51.73 (33 analysts) and the 10-year P/E median of about 37 now each rest on two sources, and the Q3 date of Oct 14 is confirmed. Valuation: the blended fair value is cut from 2,040 to 1,965 (lower 2027 multiple, a MATCH Act haircut on 2028, a base-rate anchor). I move the distribution median from about 1,930 to about 1,880 (+4%), with about 42% log-vol and Student-t (5 df) tails, so P(>=spot) goes from 0.575 to 0.545. The median sits between ASML's own conditional base rate and the peer base rate, below fair value because of late-cycle de-rating risk. Scenarios: bear 1,150 / base 1,930 / bull 2,700 at 25/50/25. No option prices or implied volatility were used. X/Twitter was not fetched; all prediction-market figures come from the Kalshi, Polymarket and Manifold public APIs as of 2026-10-01.
